title: Development and temporal validation of an explainable machine learning model for predicting in-hospital diabetic foot ulcer in patients with type 2 diabetes using inflammatory–nutritional composite in
summary: The Frontiers in Medicine study develops explainable ML models for in-hospital diabetic foot ulcer in a 550-patient cohort with a temporal validation split, a clinically specific retrospective assessment, though the validation cohort has only 18 events.
ai_technology: Logistic regression, random forest, LightGBM and XGBoost models used routinely available admission variables and inflammatory–nutritional indices to estimate in-hospital diabetic-foot-ulcer risk; LASSO selected predictors and SHAP interpreted the models.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: In 550 hospitalized patients with type 2 diabetes (400 development, 150 temporal validation), logistic regression had temporal-validation AUC 0.976, but calibration was poor (Hosmer–Lemeshow P=.001); LightGBM/XGBoost sensitivities were 0.056/0.389 at prespecified thresholds.
evidence.unknown: The temporal validation set contained 18 events; low sensitivity and calibration concerns preclude screening use. Multicenter prospective validation is still needed.
evidence.ai_role: Logistic regression, random forest, LightGBM and XGBoost models used routinely available admission variables and inflammatory–nutritional indices to estimate in-hospital diabetic-foot-ulcer risk; LASSO selected predictors and SHAP interpreted the models.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
